$comment: C23 6.10.6p4 interprets the `#line` digit sequence as a decimal integer 'ignoring any optional digit separators (6.4.4.2)'. DSS refused every such directive — ✔MEASURED through the shipped CLI: `error[P_PreprocessorDirective]: #line requires a digit sequence — got: 1'000`, with the tokenizer already lexing it as ONE token because `c.lang.json` declares `numberStyle.digitSeparator`. ★ IGNORED, NOT MERELY TOLERATED: a scan that stopped at the separator would accept the directive and renumber to 1 instead of 1000 — accepted-and-wrong, worse than the refusal it replaces — so every arm RETURNS a value derived from `__LINE__` after its directive rather than only compiling. THREE ARMS: (1) the LITERAL form with one separator; (2) the MACRO-EXPANDED form (6.10.6p6) with TWO separators, one adjacent to another, which an implementation stripping only the first scores 0 on while passing arm 1; (3) a separated digit sequence FOLLOWED by a file operand, proving the separator handling did not eat the operand after it. ✔MEASURED BY EXECUTION under -std=c2x: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both build and RUN this to exit 42, and MSVC 19.51.36252 under /std:clatest accepts the same shapes. ⚠ Under -std=c17 gcc and clang REFUSE it and are right to — digit separators are a C23 addition — which is why this is a SEPARATE example from `line_directive_macro_operand`: that one holds under C17 too, and one shared exit code could not say which rule regressed. ANTI-FOLD: the score is multiplied by a runtime `argc` predicate so the release pipeline cannot reduce main to a constant return. Data-model-independent (int arithmetic and byte comparisons only). exit = 14 * 3 = 42.
